scripts.//verify:out: Is out/ built from the source on disk? firebase.json points hosting at zipper-crm/out, so a deploy ships that directory — not git, and not whatever the last build printed. Checks freshness, probes the bundle for strings that were deleted and added, and prints artifact hashes. Run it after `npm run build` and before any hosting deploy.
scripts.//test:routing: The partner redirect table. `lib/partnerRouting.ts` has no imports and no React on purpose, so the real module compiles and runs standalone — the spec exercises the shipped code, not a copy of it.
scripts.test:routing: rm -rf .routing-test && tsc lib/partnerRouting.ts lib/partnerRouting.spec.ts --outDir .routing-test --module commonjs --target ES2020 --strict --moduleResolution node --esModuleInterop && node .routing-test/partnerRouting.spec.js; code=$?; rm -rf .routing-test; exit $code

scripts.//test:hooks: Rules of Hooks, over every component in the CRM. The agency dashboard had a useMemo and a useSecureThumbs below three conditional returns, so the hook COUNT changed between the loading render and the loaded one and React threw "Rendered more hooks than during the previous render" — which Next's GlobalError shows as "Application error: a client-side exception has occurred". The whole dashboard, blank, for every agency owner. Nothing caught it: it typechecks, it builds, and it only fails on the second render. --no-inline-config because this config loads the hooks plugin only, and the files carry eslint-disable comments for rules it does not know.
